summary.oneLiner: EIH Associated Hotels Limited, a member of The Oberoi Group, owns and operates seven luxury hotels in India under the 'Oberoi Hotels & Resorts' and 'Trident Hotels' brands.
summary.business: EIH Associated Hotels Limited is a luxury hospitality company that owns and operates seven hotels across India under the Oberoi Hotels & Resorts and Trident Hotels brands, providing accommodation, food & beverage and allied hospitality services (spa, banquets/MICE, laundry, guest transfers, loyalty programmes) to individual and group leisure travellers, corporate clients, travel agencies and event managers. The company commenced its journey in 1983 as Pleasant Hotels Limited and today operates across key business and leisure destinations in India.

currentContext.expansion: EIH Associated Hotels Limited operates seven hotels in India (784 keys) under two brands: Oberoi Hotels & Resorts (2 hotels, 146 keys — The Oberoi Rajvilas, Jaipur and The Oberoi Cecil, Shimla) and Trident Hotels (5 hotels, 638 keys — Trident Agra, Trident Bhubaneswar, Trident Jaipur, Trident Chennai and Trident Udaipur). Per the Value Creation Model disclosure, the company has one hotel in its development pipeline: a 125-room, five-star beachfront Trident Hotel under construction in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, developed in partnership with the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (APTDC) on a 40-acre beachfront site near the upcoming Bhogapuram International Airport, comprising a luxury resort and an integrated convention centre, with groundbreaking having occurred in late 2024. Within the existing portfolio: Trident Jaipur (a 127-room hotel) is undergoing a comprehensive renovation programme to re-position the property; Trident Udaipur is adding 10 luxury tents overlooking Lake Pichola, a children's activity centre and a second pool, complementing its existing inventory of 142 rooms and suites; and Trident Agra is developing a new banquet facility to expand events and conferencing capabilities for weddings, social celebrations and corporate events. Per the BRSR Principle 2 disclosure, capital expenditure incurred in FY 2025-26 on technologies to improve environmental and social impact (electric and hybrid vehicles, environment-friendly generator sets, energy-efficient LED TVs) represented 32.6% of total capex investments, up from 16.85% in FY 2024-25 (which covered LED TVs, a steam boiler, electrically operated equipment, a 500KWP solar power system and hybrid cars).

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and aviation disruption in West Asia
risks.note: Operation Sindoor in Q1 FY26 and continuing geopolitical tensions/conflict in West Asia in Q4 FY26 contributed to heightened uncertainty; management flags that resulting volatility may affect operating costs, business sentiment and travel demand in FY 2026-27, particularly inbound foreign tourism and corporate travel during the historic peak H2 period, with rising fuel prices potentially influencing airline capacity, airfares and travel patterns.

risks.risk: Regulatory cost risk from India's new Labour Codes
risks.note: The Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Relations Code 2020, Code on Social Security 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 required the Company to recognise an incremental obligation of Rs. 32.82 Million towards increased employee benefit liabilities relating to past service (booked as an Exceptional Item); the Company continues to monitor further rules and clarifications that could add incremental cost.

risks.risk: FY26 decline in revenue, margins and capital returns
risks.note: Revenue declined 5.6% y-o-y to Rs. 4,031.96 Million, EBITDA fell 4.6%, profit before tax fell 5.0% and net profit fell 4.7%, driven partly by the New Labour Code impact and closure of Trident Jaipur for renovation; Return on Capital Employed fell from 21.39% to 18.18% and Return on Equity fell from 18.38% to 15.31% year-on-year.

risks.risk: Renovation/closure-related revenue disruption in a small, concentrated hotel portfolio
risks.note: Temporary closure of Trident Jaipur for renovation was cited by the Company as a contributor to lower net profit in FY 2025-26, illustrating that with only seven owned hotels, taking any single property offline for capex/renovation has an outsized impact on overall results.

The Company's entire operations are concentrated in seven owned hotels across five Indian states (Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu) under the Oberoi Hotels & Resorts and Trident Hotels brands, so localised demand shocks, natural events or regulatory action in any one market or property can materially affect the Company.

risks.risk: Cyber and technology risk from AI-led transformation
risks.note: As the Company scales its 'ITNext' AI transformation across guest-facing and back-of-house systems and predictive data architectures, the Risk Management Committee's enterprise risk framework explicitly spans business, financial, operational, environmental, reputational, legal and cyber domains, with a dedicated Chief Risk Officer overseeing the risk programme.

risks.risk: Dependence on The Oberoi Group brand equity and standards
risks.note: The Company's identity, culture and pricing power are built entirely around membership of The Oberoi Group — operating under the licensed 'Oberoi Hotels & Resorts' and 'Trident Hotels' brands and governed by 'The Oberoi Dharma' code of conduct — making guest trust and premium positioning structurally dependent on the wider Group's brand equity and reputation.

one-line thesis: EIH Associated Hotels is India's premier luxury hotel operator with consistent RevPAR outperformance, driven by premium brand equity and resilient corporate/MICE demand. Despite FY26 revenue softening due to one-off closures and macro headwinds, the company is positioned for strong recovery via strategic renovations and new openings in high-growth corridors.

margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin: 36.0% (FY26), down from 35.7% (FY25) on higher revenue; EBITDA per available room: ₹1,762 (FY26) vs ₹1,618 (FY25); cost control maintained despite inflation

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic travel demand expected to remain the backbone of India's tourism sector, sustaining growth across leisure, weddings, MICE and spiritual tourism even amid global uncertainty affecting international travel
- Rapid expansion of India's high-income taxpayer base (Rs. 1 Crore-5 Crore bracket doubled to 2.10 lacs individuals; Rs. 5 Crore-50 Crore bracket grown from 28,000 to 50,000) significantly expanding the addressable market for luxury hospitality, with luxury stays evolving from occasional aspiration to recurring lifestyle preference
- Geographic decentralisation of affluence beyond metro hubs (Mumbai MMR, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru) into smaller cities such as Ahmedabad, Surat, Jaipur, Lucknow, Nagpur, Vadodara and Visakhapatnam, creating new feeder channels across business travel, leisure tourism, destination weddings and MICE
- India's hospitality sector positioned for another year of strong branded-supply growth, with rising hotel signings and scheduled openings reflecting sustained confidence in long-term travel demand
- Growing leisure travel driven by experiential, wellness, nature and short-break travel trends, reinforced by infrastructure investment (UDAN airport/heliport connectivity, high-speed rail corridors, PM Gati Shakti) and expanding regional air connectivity
- West Asia conflict and associated aviation disruption pose a near-term risk to inbound foreign tourism, most acutely felt at gateway properties with high international-visitor concentration (Agra, Jaipur, Kerala), though India's domestic travel base — which accounts for the preponderance of hotel demand outside a handful of gateway city properties — has shown a degree of insulation
- Rise of AI-led travel discovery is transforming how travellers plan, compare and book trips, with over 80% of Indian travellers already using AI tools for itinerary planning
- Shift toward shorter, more frequent 'stay-led' getaways is driving higher spend on premium stays, wellness, dining and curated activities as accommodation becomes central to the travel experience
- One hotel in the development pipeline per the Value Creation Model (Manufactured Capital) disclosure
- Trident Visakhapatnam: 125-room Trident hotel being developed in partnership with the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (APTDC) on a 40-acre beachfront site, comprising a luxury resort and an integrated convention centre; groundbreaking occurred in late 2024
